title: The Operational Facilitator gates whether a Root Edit proposal ever reaches a vote
content:
Per A.6.1.1.1.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.3, within seven days of submission "the Operational Facilitator must review the Root Edit Proposal for alignment" and check that the author meets the submission requirements. If aligned and eligible, the Facilitator posts the finding on the Forum and must additionally "confirm that the proposal is feasible for Operational GovOps to operationalize." If misaligned or ineligible, the Facilitator posts the finding "and provide the reasoning for it."

The consequence is stated in the next section (A.6.1.1.1.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.4): only "where their review of the proposal results in a finding of alignment" does the Facilitator trigger the Snapshot poll. Token holders therefore never vote on a proposal the Facilitator has judged misaligned — the vote is downstream of a qualitative gate, not a substitute for one.

This is a deliberate limit on token-holder sovereignty. A majority of SPK cannot enact a misaligned change because the majority is never assembled; the proposal dies at review. The mandatory public reasoning is the only counterweight — the Facilitator's discretion is checked by having to justify a rejection in writing on the Forum, not by an appeal route defined here.

The feasibility check adds a second, quieter constraint: a proposal that is aligned but cannot be operationalized by GovOps also fails to progress, which makes implementability part of admissibility.
description: Within seven days the Facilitator must certify alignment, submitter eligibility and operational feasibility; a misalignment finding stops the proposal before any poll is triggered.
